Visible logs included circuitbench-worker-protocol-4 and worker/glue/WASM paths beneath assets/1.0.0-rc.3/. The binary response was 6133055 bytes, HTTP 200, application/wasm.

Read-only SVG DOM inspection showed the expected icon plus a 'Code injected by live-server' WebSocket script. The managed preview therefore changes this asset's bytes. The separate live-host rc.2 inspection found the production icon matches the release's 443-byte body.

confirmed.result: All 17 listed files downloaded and passed the available byte/type checks. Root navigation refreshed. The page explicitly reported unavailable SHA-256 and service-worker controls on HTTP, then enabled a separate Return action. Return loaded v1.0.0-rc.3 and the preserved RC filter.

confirmed.workflow: Legacy worker bootstrap failure is actionable
confirmed.fixtureChange: The rc.3 distribution's worker alone was replaced by the exact rc.1 worker from the previous deploy archive, whose static .mjs dependency was absent.
confirmed.result: The browser reproduced an opaque worker-startup failure. The new adapter inspected the exact worker URL and reported HTTP 200, text/javascript, and missing circuitbench-worker-protocol-4, identifying an older/different response as a possibility. No numerical result was accepted.
Returning to the unmodified root rc.3 page and running again completed 501 AC points at revision 7; waveform view and baseline overlay were visible.

limitations: Ordinary HTTP prevents actual browser service-worker installation, secure cache removal and SHA-256 API use in this preview. VM tests exercise those paths separately; no secure or offline browser pass is claimed.

The production-layout browser recovery correctly reported 17/18 because the preview injected script into SVG. The controlled success fixture does not substitute for complete production-host recovery verification.
The user's actual no-message bootstrap failure was not reproduced at the live HTTPS host in a clean browser. Live rc.2 runs succeeded; stale browser/CDN bytes remain an inference.
